issues.legal_issue: A lease granted by a mortgagor in possession after the mortgage binds the mortgagee only when it is made in the ordinary course of management.
material_facts: The mortgage was created before the lease was granted, and the mortgagor remained in possession.
The mortgagor granted a permanent lease of the mortgaged villages.
The lessees did not allege or establish that the lease was granted on usual terms in the ordinary course of management.
The mortgagee’s successor purchased the mortgaged property at an execution sale and sought possession from the lessees.
issues.conclusion: The permanent lease was not binding on the mortgagee’s successor, and the successor was entitled to possession.
issues.legal_principle: For leases granted before section 65-A of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, the mortgagor in possession could bind the mortgagee by dealing with the property in the usual course of management, as an agent or bailiff might. A lease on unusual terms, or one that changes the character or use of the property, does not bind the mortgagee merely because it does not impair the security; section 66, which concerns waste, does not govern the power to lease. The lessee bears the burden of establishing that the lease was made on usual terms in the ordinary course of management. The Court approved Madan Mohan Singh v. Raj Kishore Kumari (1916) 21 C.W.N. 88, dissented from Balmukund v. Motilal (1915) 20 C.W.N. 350, and explained Banee Pershad v. Beet Bhunjun Singh (1868) 10 W.R. 325. It also referred to Corbett v. Plowden, Pope v. Briggs, and Moreland v. Richardson in describing the mortgagee’s paramount position and the mortgagor’s authority in ordinary management.

rule.if: mortgagee_possession_claim and mortgage_preceded_lease and mortgagor_in_possession and lessee_failed_usual_management_proof

predicates.mortgagee_possession_claim: A mortgagee or a successor to the mortgagee seeks possession against a person claiming under a lease granted by the mortgagor.
predicates.mortgage_preceded_lease: The lease was granted after the mortgage was created.
predicates.mortgagor_in_possession: The mortgagor remained in possession when the lease was granted.
predicates.lessee_failed_usual_management_proof: The lessee did not establish that the lease was on usual terms and made in the ordinary course of management.

issues.definition: When a mortgagee or successor seeks possession under these circumstances, failure by the lessee to establish ordinary-course management means the lease does not bind the mortgagee or successor.
